answer: Trust propagates from trusted anchors through bounded-length random walks on the attestation graph, with transition weights normalized and voting mass charged only when reached from those anchors. A sybil cluster separated by a sparse external cut has low conductance, limiting the probability that walks enter it; thus its aggregate voting weight is bounded by cut capacity and seed mass, not by the number of fabricated identities. A violet-labeled node or sonnet-tagged edge changes nothing without trusted connectivity.
